sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是《99%隐形》。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: In southwest Alaska, two big rivers flow across the subarctic tundra, emptying into the Bering Sea.
sentences.zh: 在阿拉斯加西南部，两条大河横穿亚北极苔原，汇入白令海。

sentences.en: Together, the rivers create the Yukon-Kuskokwim Delta, an area the size of the state of Illinois.
sentences.zh: 这两条河共同造就了育空-库斯科奎姆三角洲，其面积相当于伊利诺伊州的大小。

sentences.en: Scattered along the rivers and coast are 56 Alaska Native tribes in communities of mostly a few hundred people.
sentences.zh: 沿河和海岸散布着56个阿拉斯加原住民部落，每个社区大多只有几百人。

sentences.en: The Tundra River Delta is a wetland, with ponds scattered in every direction and streams and tributaries braiding and weaving between them.
sentences.zh: 苔原河三角洲是一片湿地，池塘星罗棋布，溪流和支流在其中交织穿梭。

sentences.en: That's reporter Anna Rose MacArthur, who lives in the YK Delta.
sentences.zh: 那是记者安娜·罗斯·麦克阿瑟，她就住在育空-库斯科奎姆三角洲。

sentences.en: From an airplane, it's hard to tell if there's more water or land below.
sentences.zh: 从飞机上看，很难分辨下面到底是水多还是陆地多。

sentences.en: It's really beautiful.
sentences.zh: 真的很美。

sentences.en: The hub of this region is the city of Bethel, population 6,500.
sentences.zh: 该地区的中心是伯特利市，人口6500人。

sentences.en: The town is the economic and bureaucratic center of the Delta.
sentences.zh: 这座城镇是三角洲的经济和行政中心。

sentences.en: It's the place people fly into for medical care, shopping, and work.
sentences.zh: 人们乘飞机来到这里就医、购物和工作。

sentences.en: And the reason they fly is because the entire region is off the road system.
sentences.zh: 他们之所以乘飞机，是因为整个地区都没有公路系统。

sentences.en: That means that, while there are roads within communities, there are no roads connecting towns like Bethel to the outside.
sentences.zh: 这意味着，虽然社区内部有道路，但没有公路将伯特利这样的城镇与外界连接起来。

sentences.en: The land is too boggy to support them.
sentences.zh: 这里的土地太泥泞，无法支撑公路建设。

sentences.en: The interstates and highways that link most towns and cities in North America don't exist here.
sentences.zh: 北美大多数城镇和城市之间连接的州际公路和高速公路，在这里并不存在。

sentences.en: The only way in or out of any of the communities in the region, including Bethel, is by plane or boat.
sentences.zh: 进出该地区任何社区（包括伯特利）的唯一方式就是乘飞机或船。

sentences.en: In winter, you can also snowmobile or drive a truck along the frozen river, which we call the Ice Highway.
sentences.zh: 冬天，你也可以骑雪地摩托或开卡车沿着冰封的河流行驶，我们称之为“冰上高速公路”。

sentences.en: And that presents some interesting challenges when it comes to waste.
sentences.zh: 这在处理垃圾方面带来了一些有趣的挑战。

sentences.en: Because pretty much everything that gets imported into Bethel ultimately stays in Bethel.
sentences.zh: 因为几乎所有进口到伯特利的东西，最终都会留在伯特利。

sentences.en: It comes in by cargo plane or barge.
sentences.zh: 它们是通过货运飞机或驳船运进来的。

sentences.en: And even when something stops working, it's often too expensive and too inconvenient to get it out again.
sentences.zh: 即使某样东西坏了，想要把它运出去也往往太昂贵、太麻烦了。

sentences.en: In other places in the United States, trash is thrown away.
sentences.zh: 在美国的其他地方，垃圾会被丢弃。

sentences.en: But in a town scratched from the tundra, unconnected by roads, there is no away.
sentences.zh: 但在这样一个从苔原上开辟出来、没有公路连接的城镇里，根本没有“丢弃”这回事。

sentences.en: There is only here.
sentences.zh: 只有“留在这里”。

sentences.en: And so junk slowly accumulates.
sentences.zh: 于是，垃圾慢慢堆积起来。

sentences.en: People's yards fill with wooden pallets, fishing buoys, oil drums, and tarps with mysterious stuff underneath.
sentences.zh: 人们的院子里堆满了木托盘、渔业浮标、油桶，还有盖着神秘物品的防水布。

sentences.en: It's a common sight throughout rural Alaska.
sentences.zh: 这在阿拉斯加农村地区是很常见的景象。

sentences.en: And there's no social stigma attached.
sentences.zh: 而且这并没有什么社会污名。

sentences.en: No neighborhood committee policing acceptable lawn decor.
sentences.zh: 没有社区委员会来监管草坪装饰是否得体。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So this is rolling.
sentences.zh: 现在开始录音了。

sentences.en: Oh, it is?
sentences.zh: 噢，是吗？

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Other people might not see all this junk as a problem.
sentences.zh: 其他人可能并不觉得这些垃圾是个问题。

sentences.en: But then there's Diane McCachron.
sentences.zh: 但戴安·麦卡克伦不这么看。

sentences.en: She's my roommate.
sentences.zh: 她是我的室友。

sentences.en: She's lived in Bethel for more than 20 years.
sentences.zh: 她在伯特利住了20多年了。

sentences.en: And she's a very self-motivated person, prone to eccentric obsessions and quests.
sentences.zh: 她是一个非常有主见的人，容易产生古怪的执念和追求。

sentences.en: Now, okay, should I put her in the house?
sentences.zh: 好了，我是不是该把她关进屋里？

sentences.en: Because there's going to be, she might do some dog barking.
sentences.zh: 因为可能会有……她可能会让狗叫起来。

sentences.en: Yeah, that'll be a good idea.
sentences.zh: 嗯，那是个好主意。

sentences.en: Let me do that.
sentences.zh: 我来处理。

sentences.en: Diane has biked 2,000 miles solo across the United States, twice.
sentences.zh: 戴安曾独自骑行横穿美国2000英里，而且是两次。

sentences.en: She's been arrested for political activism and has been known to stick anti-war flyers
sentences.zh: 她曾因政治活动被捕，还曾因在杂货店的汤罐头和麦片盒之间

sentences.en: between cans of soup and cereal boxes at the grocery store.
sentences.zh: 塞入反战传单而闻名。

sentences.en: She also curates a photo collection of Bethel's overflowing dumpsters that she finds amusing.
sentences.zh: 她还专门收集伯特利那些溢出来的垃圾桶的照片，她觉得这很有趣。

sentences.en: We have to decide the first place.
sentences.zh: 我们得先定好第一个地点。

sentences.en: And about a year ago, her eccentric obsession fixated on something that many people don't notice,
sentences.zh: 大约一年前，她那古怪的执念锁定在了一个许多人根本注意不到的东西上，

sentences.en: for the same reason that fish don't notice water.
sentences.zh: 就像鱼儿注意不到水一样。

sentences.en: Diane became obsessed with the most visible manifestation of the town's junk problem,
sentences.zh: 戴安开始痴迷于该镇垃圾问题最明显的表现形式，

sentences.en: the dead cars.
sentences.zh: 那就是废弃车辆。

sentences.en: If you care to notice, you see them everywhere.
sentences.zh: 如果你愿意留意，你会发现它们随处可见。

sentences.en: Broken down, abandoned, left to rust and rot out in the elements.
sentences.zh: 抛锚的、废弃的，任由它们在风吹雨打中生锈腐烂。

sentences.en: The kinds of areas that dead cars get located.
sentences.zh: 废弃车辆出现的区域五花八门。

sentences.en: Homes, random parking lots, totally offbeat locations, places of business.
sentences.zh: 住宅、随意的停车场、完全偏僻的地方、商业场所。

sentences.en: Dead cars line the sides of the roads.
sentences.zh: 废弃车辆排在路边。

sentences.en: They fill people's yards and sit scattered throughout public parking lots.
sentences.zh: 它们填满了人们的院子，散落在公共停车场里。

sentences.en: And Diane has decided she wants to count them all.
sentences.zh: 戴安决定要把它们全部数出来。

sentences.en: So, she's divided Bethel into sections.
sentences.zh: 于是，她把伯特利分成了若干区域。

sentences.en: Over the course of a year, she's methodically checked every street, parking lot, and yard.
sentences.zh: 在过去的一年里，她按部就班地检查了每一条街道、停车场和院子。

sentences.en: And I've been tagging along.
sentences.zh: 而我一直跟着她。

sentences.en: Let the clicking begin!
sentences.zh: 开始计数吧！

sentences.en: She bought one of those handheld clickers, a little silver one, like the kind used to count the number of people attending events.
sentences.zh: 她买了一个手持计数器，银色的小东西，就像那种用来统计活动参加人数的计数器。

sentences.en: Or to count anything, really.
sentences.zh: 或者说，用来统计任何东西。

sentences.en: So, there's the SUV, an SUV next to it, Ford, Ford, Ford.
sentences.zh: 看，那有一辆SUV，旁边还有一辆SUV，福特，福特，福特。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: We're up to 67, and we have not hit a neighborhood yet.
sentences.zh: 我们已经数到67辆了，而且还没进到居民区呢。

sentences.en: So.
sentences.zh: 所以。

sentences.en: Diane sees the dead cars as a symptom of something bigger.
sentences.zh: 戴安认为这些废弃车辆是一个更大问题的征兆。

sentences.en: About 100 vehicles were taken to the Bethel landfill last year.
sentences.zh: 去年大约有100辆车被送到了伯特利垃圾填埋场。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, about 300 vehicles were barged into town.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，大约有300辆车通过驳船运进了城里。

sentences.en: All these cars are coming in, but they're not going out.
sentences.zh: 所有的车都在源源不断地进来，却没能出去。

sentences.en: And they're piling up around us.
sentences.zh: 它们在我们周围越堆越多。

sentences.en: We're not going to get away with this for forever.
sentences.zh: 我们不可能永远逃避这个问题。

sentences.en: I mean, there's a price to be paid for this kind of materialism, of which I'm part of.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这种物质主义是有代价的，而我本身也是其中的一部分。

sentences.en: So, I'm not, like, saying I'm exempt, because I'm not.
sentences.zh: 所以，我并不是说我能置身事外，因为我不能。

sentences.en: I give it a lot of thought, though.
sentences.zh: 不过，我确实对此思考了很多。

sentences.en: And how can we organize ourselves to handle this differently is sort of a burning question for me.
sentences.zh: 我们该如何组织起来以不同的方式处理这个问题，对我来说是一个迫切的问题。

sentences.en: Now, that red truck doesn't look right, does it?
sentences.zh: 现在，那辆红色的卡车看起来不太对劲，是吧？

sentences.en: Click.
sentences.zh: 咔哒。

sentences.en: I love living in Bethel.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢住在伯特利。

sentences.en: I love its small city intimacy.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢它小城市般的亲密感。

sentences.en: I love that I can walk in any direction and, in a couple miles, pitch a tent in the tundra wilderness.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢我可以朝任何方向走，走上几英里，就能在苔原荒野中搭起帐篷。

sentences.en: I love that a two-minute stop is considered a traffic jam.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢这里两分钟的停留就被视为交通堵塞。

sentences.en: I love fishing for salmon in the summer, picking wild berries in the fall, and cheering for sled dog races in the winter.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢夏天钓鲑鱼，秋天采摘野果，冬天为雪橇犬比赛加油助威。

sentences.en: But this town, it isn't for everyone.
sentences.zh: 但这个城镇并不适合所有人。

sentences.en: Just go to the airport, and you'll see.
sentences.zh: 去机场看看就知道了。

sentences.en: Okay, so here we are.
sentences.zh: 好了，我们到了。

sentences.en: We're at the lot across from the main terminal.
sentences.zh: 我们在主航站楼对面的停车场。

sentences.en: The Bethel airport is where the town's dead car problem is most apparent.
sentences.zh: 伯特利机场是该镇废弃车辆问题最明显的地方。

sentences.en: It's like a graveyard of rusting vehicles.
sentences.zh: 它就像一个生锈车辆的坟场。

sentences.en: There are rumors the cars were left by people who just drove to the airport, got on a plane, and never looked back.
sentences.zh: 有传言说，这些车是那些开车到机场，坐上飞机就再也没回来的人留下的。

sentences.en: And it's so bad, you can almost never find a parking space.
sentences.zh: 情况太糟糕了，你几乎永远找不到停车位。

sentences.en: This one is dead and double parked.
sentences.zh: 这一辆已经报废了，还占了两个车位。

sentences.en: That's like a middle finger to the town.
sentences.zh: 这就像是对这个城镇竖中指。

sentences.en: It's like, I'm going to leave this car here, and I'm going to double parked.
sentences.zh: 就像是在说，我要把车留在这儿，而且我要占两个车位。

sentences.en: I'm going to take up two spaces while I do it.
sentences.zh: 我占两个车位又怎样。

sentences.en: And look at the body.
sentences.zh: 看看这车身。

sentences.en: That body is excellent.
sentences.zh: 这车身状况真好。

sentences.en: The Alaska Department of Transportation oversees the Bethel airport, and between keeping snow off the runways and filling potholes,
sentences.zh: 阿拉斯加交通部负责管理伯特利机场，除了清理跑道上的积雪和填补坑洼之外，

sentences.en: removing abandoned cars hasn't been their priority, which means the cars keep accumulating.
sentences.zh: 清理废弃车辆一直不是他们的优先事项，这意味着车辆不断堆积。

sentences.en: And now they're a major headache.
sentences.zh: 现在它们成了一个大麻烦。

sentences.en: Okay, first of all, with the airport here in Bethel, have you been out to Bethel and seen the layout?
sentences.zh: 好的，首先，关于伯特利的机场，你去过伯特利并看过那里的布局吗？

sentences.en: It's, you know, it's been a long time, but yes, I have been out there.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道，那是很久以前的事了，但是的，我去过那里。

sentences.en: Shannon McCarthy is a spokesperson for the Alaska Department of Transportation.
sentences.zh: 香农·麦卡锡是阿拉斯加交通部的发言人。

sentences.en: If it becomes obvious to us that a car has been abandoned, and oftentimes you'll see, like, lots of snow on it or, you know, lots of dust on it, that kind of thing,
sentences.zh: 如果我们明显看出车辆已被遗弃，而且通常你会看到上面积满了雪，或者积满了灰尘之类的，

sentences.en: they are required to, you know, post it for removal for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 我们必须依法张贴通知，要求在30天内移走。

sentences.en: And then once the 30 days has passed, we actually have to bring them to our shop, and we have to prepare them just for disposal.
sentences.zh: 30天过后，我们实际上必须把它们带到我们的修理厂，并为报废做准备。

sentences.en: That means draining the fluids, removing the battery, and taking the vehicle to the dump.
sentences.zh: 这意味着排干液体、拆除电池，然后把车送到垃圾场。

sentences.en: That's the proper way to dispose of a car in Bethel.
sentences.zh: 这就是在伯特利处理报废车辆的正确方式。

sentences.en: It costs the state $50 for each car they have to deal with, because the owners are nowhere to be found.
sentences.zh: 州政府处理每辆车要花费50美元，因为车主根本找不到。

sentences.en: You know, we do try to make contact, but oftentimes if someone is disposing of a vehicle clandestinely,
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们确实尝试过联系，但如果有人是偷偷摸摸地处理车辆，

sentences.en: if you will, they oftentimes don't leave good contact information, you know, or the contact information no longer is valid.
sentences.zh: 如果可以这么说的话，他们通常不会留下有效的联系方式，或者联系方式已经失效了。

sentences.en: So, unfortunately, we're not able to recoup those costs very frequently.
sentences.zh: 所以很遗憾，我们很难收回这些成本。

sentences.en: Oh, my.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: Just so you know, we're up to 188 cars.
sentences.zh: 告诉你，我们已经数到188辆车了。

sentences.en: What?
sentences.zh: 什么？

sentences.en: We haven't even, still haven't really scratched the surface of Bethel.
sentences.zh: 我们甚至还没真正触及伯特利的皮毛呢。

sentences.en: Let's go over the signs again, like the telltale signs that distinguish the car.
sentences.zh: 让我们再复习一下这些迹象，也就是区分报废车辆的明显特征。

sentences.en: There's grass growing up around the tires, and the grass is tall enough that it took a while for the grass to begin growing.
sentences.zh: 轮胎周围长满了草，而且草长得很高，说明这些草长出来花了不少时间。

sentences.en: Of course, the real obvious, pancake tires.
sentences.zh: 当然，最明显的就是瘪掉的轮胎。

sentences.en: Tires that are completely off the rim.
sentences.zh: 轮胎完全脱离了轮毂。

sentences.en: The windows are all broken out.
sentences.zh: 车窗全部破碎。

sentences.en: And then maybe I know that that car has never moved for a year.
sentences.zh: 还有，我可能知道那辆车已经一年没动过了。

sentences.en: Or it's sunken into the dirt.
sentences.zh: 或者它已经陷进了泥土里。

sentences.en: Oh, yeah, it's started to sink into, sink into earth itself.
sentences.zh: 噢，是的，它已经开始下陷，陷进大地本身了。

sentences.en: That's the sad thing.
sentences.zh: 这才是最可悲的。

sentences.en: Oh, oh, look at that beautiful Chevy.
sentences.zh: 噢，噢，看那辆漂亮的雪佛兰。

sentences.en: That beautiful color.
sentences.zh: 那颜色真漂亮。

sentences.en: Not all dead cars in Bethel are abandoned and left for someone else to deal with, like the ones at the airport.
sentences.zh: 伯特利并非所有的废弃车辆都是被遗弃并留给别人处理的，就像机场里的那些一样。

sentences.en: Some are carefully curated, meant to be used for a greater purpose in the future.
sentences.zh: 有些是经过精心挑选的，打算在未来用于更大的用途。

sentences.en: Like the cars beside Aggie Gregory's house.
sentences.zh: 比如阿吉·格雷戈里家旁边的那些车。

sentences.en: Okay, so will you tell me the story about these cars in the yard?
sentences.zh: 好的，你能给我讲讲院子里这些车的故事吗？

sentences.en: There's three that are just sitting on our property, and a couple of them are the same.
sentences.zh: 有三辆就停在我们的地盘上，其中有几辆是同款的。

sentences.en: And so we use one for parts for the other one.
sentences.zh: 所以我们用其中一辆作为另一辆的零件车。

sentences.en: Dead cars are a common feature in yards here, because cannibalizing parts to fix other vehicles happens all the time.
sentences.zh: 废弃车辆在院子里很常见，因为拆卸零件来修理其他车辆的情况时有发生。

sentences.en: And so, wait, is that the one that you're supposed to fix up, the silver one?
sentences.zh: 等等，那辆银色的就是你打算修理的那辆吗？

sentences.en: We're supposed to, but I don't know if that's going to ever happen.
sentences.zh: 我们是打算修的，但我不知道这是否真的会发生。

sentences.en: If you don't get it fixed up, how long do you think it's going to sit there?
sentences.zh: 如果你不把它修好，你觉得它会停在那里多久？

sentences.en: That's a good question.
sentences.zh: 这是个好问题。

sentences.en: Aggie says that they eventually want to get rid of the cars so they have room to park their old boat,
sentences.zh: 阿吉说他们最终想把这些车处理掉，腾出地方停他们的旧船，

sentences.en: because they plan to get a new boat and strip the old one for parts.
sentences.zh: 因为他们计划买一艘新船，并把旧船拆了当零件用。

sentences.en: They have two snowmobiles for the same reason.
sentences.zh: 他们有两辆雪地摩托也是出于同样的原因。

sentences.en: Some parts are, it's harder to get, I guess, and it costs money to ship, and so why not keep them and use them?
sentences.zh: 有些零件比较难买，我想，而且运输成本很高，所以为什么不留着它们用呢？

sentences.en: Rural Alaska is famous for its scrappy resourcefulness.
sentences.zh: 阿拉斯加农村地区以其精打细算的足智多谋而闻名。

sentences.en: You can't live in a place that's so remote, where things take so long to get, and cost so much money without creativity.
